tsa-a18-v01.quick_english: One well-practised in knowledge should be consecrated to be a practitioner, or a teacher — for even devoid of all marks, the knower alone is entitled to practitionerhood and to grace-bestowing; not another, even if consecrated.

tsa-a18-v02.quick_english: Having handed over his own authority, a teacher who performs no initiation incurs no fault; but before that, by fault, by authority-bond, by the Vidyeśa-state-giving one, bondage itself is his non-performance of initiation. So consecrated, for mantra-deity-identity success, six-monthly, daily, by muttering-fire-offering-special-worship conduct, let him do the knowledge-vow. Thereafter, having attained being-made-of-that, he is entitled in initiation and the rest. Therein: the unfit let him not initiate, nor let him shun the fit; even the initiated let him test in knowledge-giving; knowing even deceit-grasped knowledge, let him overlook it; and herein, by consecration-splendor, god-worship and the rest.

tsa-a18-v01.speaker: Teacher (injunction)
tsa-a18-v01.question: Who is to be consecrated, and why?
premises: Consecrate the well-practised knower as practitioner or guru.
The knower alone, even markless, is entitled to practitionerhood and grace-bestowing; no other, even consecrated.
tsa-a18-v01.inference: Entitlement follows knowledge, not marks and not prior consecration: the markless knower alone is fit for practitionerhood or guruhood.

tsa-a18-v02.speaker: Teacher (discipline)
tsa-a18-v02.question: What binds, what frees, what disciplines the consecrated?
premises: The guru who has handed over authority incurs no fault by not initiating; before that, non-initiating IS bondage.
The consecrated does the six-month vidyāvrata for mantra-deity identity; then, that-made, he is entitled to initiate.
Test the unfit out, never shun the fit; test even the initiated; overlook known deceit; worship by consecration-splendor.
tsa-a18-v02.inference: Delegation ends the duty to initiate; before it, omission binds. The consecrated earns initiation-rights through vidyāvrata, then examines strictly and overlooks knowingly.

tsa-a18-v01.plain_english: One well-practised in knowledge should be consecrated, to be a practitioner or a teacher — for even devoid of all marks, the knower alone is entitled to practitionerhood and to bestowing grace; not another, even if consecrated.
tsa-a18-v01.sanskrit_cite: svabhyastajñāninaṃ sādhakatve gurutve vā abhiṣiñcet yataḥ sarvalakṣaṇahīno 'pi jñānavān eva sādhakatve anugrahakaraṇe ca adhikṛtaḥ na anyaḥ abhiṣikto 'pi

tsa-a18-v02.plain_english: Having handed over his own authority, a teacher who performs no initiation incurs no fault; but before that, bondage itself, through fault, through authority's bond, through the giver of the Vidyeśa state, is his non-performance of initiation. So consecrated, for the success of mantra-deity identity, six-monthly, daily, through the conduct of muttering, fire-offering, and special worship, let him perform the knowledge-vow. Thereafter, having become made of that, he is entitled in initiation and the rest. Therein: let him not initiate the unfit, nor let him pass over the fit; let him test even the initiated in the giving of knowledge; having known even deceit-grasped knowledge, let him overlook it; and herein, through the splendor of consecration, god-worship and the rest.
tsa-a18-v02.sanskrit_cite: svādhikārasamarpaṇe guruḥ dīkṣādi akurvan api na pratyavaiti pūrvaṃ tu pratyavāyena adhikārabandhena vidyeśapadadāyinā bandha eva asya dīkṣādyakaraṇam so 'bhiṣikto mantradevatātādātmyasiddhaye ṣāṇmāsikaṃ pratyahaṃ japahomaviśeṣapūjācaraṇena vidyāvrataṃ kuryāt tadanantaraṃ labdhatanmayībhāvo dīkṣādau adhikṛtaḥ tatra na ayogyān dīkṣeta na ca yogyaṃ pariharet dīkṣitam api jñānadāne parīkṣeta chadmagṛhītajñānam api jñātvā upekṣeta atra ca abhiṣekavibhavena devapūjādikam

essence: Consecrate the practiced knower as practitioner or teacher: knowing alone entitles; marks or prior consecration do not.
Delegation ends the duty to initiate; before it, omission binds. The consecrated earns initiation-rights through vidyāvrata, then examines strictly and overlooks knowingly.

rasa.justification: Two injunctions and their reasons, stated once each, never raised: the stillness is in the command's economy.

sections.SUMMARY: Consecrate the practiced knower as practitioner or teacher: knowing alone entitles; marks or prior consecration do not. Delegation ends the duty to initiate; before it, omission binds. The consecrated earns initiation-rights through six months of daily vidyāvrata for mantra-deity identity; then, made of That, examines strictly — tests the unfit out, never shuns the fit, tests even the taught, overlooks knowing deceit, and worships by consecration-splendor.
sections.FUNCTION: Sets who may be consecrated, when the duty to initiate ends, and how the consecrated prove and examine.
sections.KEY TERMS: svabhyastajñānin (well-practised knower as the only qualification); adhikāra (entitlement as knowing, not office); abhiṣeka (consecration as handing over); vidyāvrata (six-month knowledge-vow); tanmayībhāva (made-of-That as initiation-right); parīkṣā/upekṣā (testing and overlooking as the two disciplines).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Eighteenth āhnika, second in the gold sequence: entitlement stated, delegation defined, then the vow and the examinations.
sections.BOUNDARY: No rite is described in full; only who, when, and how examined.
sections.EXPLANATION: The āhnika answers three questions. Who may be consecrated: the well-practised knower, as practitioner or teacher — knowing alone entitles, with or without marks, and no one else, even already consecrated. When the duty to initiate ends: once the guru has handed over his own authority, non-initiating incurs no fault; before that handover, the very omission is bondage, through fault, authority-bond, and the Vidyeśa-state-giver. How the consecrated proceed: six months of daily muttering, fire-offering, and special worship as knowledge-vow for mantra-deity identity; then, made of That, entitled to initiate — testing the unfit out, never shunning the fit, testing even the initiated in knowledge-giving, overlooking known deceit-borne knowledge, and worshipping gods by consecration-splendor.
sections.RELATED: Pradipaka ch.18 rite (same text, free rendering — support only); Vishvasa ch.18 (same); Wallis/Ferrario on abhiṣeka/adhikāra (guru-making context).

lines: Consecrate the well-practised knower — as practitioner, as teacher.
Marks or no marks: knowing alone entitles;
to practising, to grace-giving. No other —
not even the consecrated, if knowing is absent.

Before that handing-over, fault itself, bond-of-authority, the Vidyeśa-state-giver —

six months, daily, muttering, fire, special worship —
do the knowledge-vow, for mantra-deity identity;
made of That, initiate. Test the unfit out, never pass the fit;
test even the taught in teachings given; overlook known deceit;
by splendor of anointing, worship gods and the rest.

lines: Consecrate the knowing-practised — practitioner or teacher be he;
marks or markless, knowing alone entitles —
to practising, to grace-giving. No other:
not even the anointed, if knowing is absent.
